worlds.research_question: Determine why the same customer-support AI system has lower answer quality in Region B than Region A, whether retrieval-cache behavior is the primary driver, and which competing explanations should be retained.

catalog.descriptor: Repeat matched requests under the same deployment conditions
Perturb one operating condition around the current baseline
Test whether one simple proposed mechanism alone explains the regional gap
Run a controlled intervention on the suspected retrieval-cache factor
Inspect a boundary subgroup where the regional gap may differ
Audit the reliability of the answer-quality measurement
Run robustness checks under alternative exclusions and scoring choices

modules.U3: Across 10 matched daily windows with identical request categories, Region B remains 7-11% lower on the frozen quality score. Region A was already about 2% higher before the latest cache configuration change.
modules.G8: When request complexity and traffic load are perturbed in matched replay tests, the regional gap ranges from 4% to 10%; it is largest at high retrieval depth and smallest for simple no-retrieval requests.
modules.S4: Longer conversation histories are more common in Region B. Matching on history length reduces the regional quality gap by about 1.5 percentage points but leaves a residual gap.
modules.W1: During two windows when retrieval caching was disabled in both regions, Region B still scored about 5% lower. Cache availability alone therefore does not explain the full regional difference.
modules.E7: A randomized cache-policy crossover on 1,200 replayed requests improved Region B quality by 3.8 percentage points, 95% CI 2.1 to 5.5, with little change in Region A.
modules.Y5: The gap is near zero for single-turn FAQ requests but 9-12% for multi-turn requests requiring retrieval across two or more documents.
modules.D2: Independent human raters show inter-rater kappa 0.86 on the quality rubric. An audit found Region B has 3% more missing citation metadata, which can lower the automated score by roughly 0.5 percentage points.
modules.K9: Across alternative scoring rubrics, removal of citation penalties, and matched-history analyses, the cache-policy effect remains 3-5 points while a residual Region B deficit of 2-5 points persists.

worlds.research_question: Determine why Assembly Line B has a higher defect rate than Line A, whether the new torque tool is the primary driver, and which competing explanations should be retained.

catalog.descriptor: Run a controlled intervention on the suspected torque-tool factor
Audit the reliability of defect measurement and classification
Perturb one operating condition around the current baseline
Run robustness checks under alternative exclusions and matching choices
Repeat matched production runs under the same nominal conditions
Test whether one simple proposed mechanism alone explains the line gap
Inspect a boundary subgroup where the defect gap may differ

modules.C2: Across 12 matched production weeks, Line B has a defect rate 3.5-5.8 percentage points above Line A. Line B was already about 1.2 points worse before the new torque tool was installed.
modules.A9: Under matched speed and product-mix conditions, the line gap ranges from 1.5 to 5 points and becomes largest during high-throughput periods.
modules.R8: Line B has more newly assigned operators and more frequent shift handovers. Matching on operator tenure and handover frequency reduces the estimated line gap by about 1 point.
modules.V7: On three shifts when the new torque tool was taken offline and the prior tool was used, Line B still had a defect rate about 2.4 points above Line A. The tool alone does not explain the whole gap.
modules.H6: A randomized crossover of 80 assemblies between the new and prior torque tools reduced torque-related defects by 2.0 percentage points with the new tool, 95% CI 0.6 to 3.4.
modules.L1: The line gap is near zero for low-torque assemblies but 5-7 points for high-torque assemblies with multi-stage fastening.
modules.P3: Independent inspectors agree on defect classification 96% of the time. A calibration audit found one sensor on Line B overflags borderline torque defects by about 0.6 percentage points.
modules.N4: After excluding borderline sensor cases, matching operator tenure, and stratifying product mix, the new-tool effect remains 1.5-2.5 points while a residual Line B disadvantage of 1-3 points persists.
